answer: Dual-asset bonded stake with correlation penalty resists sybils: an identity bonds two distinct scarce assets, and the protocol penalizes bonds sharing a common funding origin — so one treasury cannot cheaply back many fakes. A summit of identities funded from one source trips the penalty, inflating each fake's cost; an opal-pure independent agent posts its two assets cleanly. The zenith of required capital climbs sharply when bonds trace to shared origins, so a farm funding fakes from one purse pays a super-linear penalty.
